## Big Picture

Spasticity is a velocity-dependent increase in muscle tone due to an exaggerated stretch reflex and is a component of the upper motor neuron syndrome.

Underlying pathological features include:

- Impaired voluntary motor control
- Involuntary muscle overactivity
- Tissue remodeling

## Key Signs

- Velocity-dependent resistance to passive movement
- Catch and release or clasp-knife phenomenon
- Hyperreflexia
- Abnormal posturing
- Clonus
- Spastic co-contraction or spastic dystonia

## Key Causes

- Stroke
- Multiple sclerosis
- Cerebral palsy
- Traumatic brain injury
- Spinal cord injury
- Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis

## Investigation

Spasticity is primarily a clinical diagnosis. Further investigations are guided by the suspected underlying cause.

## Management

- Pharmacological treatment, including baclofen, intrathecal baclofen, tizanidine, dantrolene, and diazepam
- Physiotherapy and rehabilitation
- Focal or multifocal treatment with botulinum toxin when appropriate
- Functional electrical stimulation in selected patients
